title: Saudi Arabia | SAMA Financial Consumer Protection and Conduct
tagline: Apply SAMA's consumer protection, conduct, complaints, debt collection and confidentiality rules at a conventional Saudi bank.
sectors: Conventional commercial banks in Saudi Arabia
Foreign bank branches in Saudi Arabia
Bank call centres and outsourced service providers
Debt collection agencies acting for banks
description:
This quest teaches the consumer protection and conduct rules the **Saudi Central Bank (SAMA)** sets for conventional banks. It is based on SAMA's **Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules** (2022), the **Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions** (2019), the **Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures** (2025), the **Account Opening Rules**, the **Instructions for Services Provided to Persons with Disabilities**, the **Regulations for Establishing Customer Care Departments in Banks** and the **Control and Awareness Measures for Branch and Customer Service Employees**, all published in the SAMA Rulebook.

Rule 14 of the consumer protection rules requires banks to train front-line staff on a regular basis and make sure they hold the required professional certificates. Other instruments require tellers and customer service staff to complete KYC, AML/CFT and ethics courses before taking up their posts, awareness campaigns for branch and customer service staff at least every three months with tests every six months, and proof that bank and agency collectors know the collection policy. This quest supports those duties for branch, call-centre, customer care, credit and collection staff and their managers.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own policies, procedures or the latest SAMA instructions; always follow them. It covers conventional banking only.
audience: Tellers, customer service and account opening staff at conventional banks in Saudi Arabia
Call-centre and customer care staff, including agents contracted through third parties
Retail credit officers, branch managers and collection staff, and managers of agencies collecting for banks
Customer Care Department, compliance and internal audit staff who monitor fair treatment
outcomes: Explain SAMA's ten consumer protection principles and the training, certificate and monitoring duties in Rules 14 and 15
Apply SAMA's disclosure, document, notice and account opening rules at the counter
Handle complaints within SAMA's channels, timelines and records rules, and serve persons with disabilities and vulnerable customers fairly
Collect debts within the 2025 regulations on contact, objections, deductions, rescheduling and the Article 10 collection policy
Apply SAMA's conduct, gifts and confidentiality principles and the three-monthly awareness and six-monthly testing measures
Assemble the training, monitoring and audit evidence a SAMA review expects

sessions.title: SAMA's Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Who Must Be Trained
sessions.summary: Meet SAMA's 2022 Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules: who they protect, the ten principles, the general conduct rules, and Rules 14 and 15, which require regular training, professional certificates and monitoring of front-line staff.
objectives: Explain the legal basis, scope and purpose of SAMA's Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules
Apply the ten consumer protection principles to everyday branch and call-centre decisions
Describe Rule 14 (conduct, regular training and certificates for front-line staff) and Rule 15 (monitoring visits)
Identify which staff need the retail banking and credit adviser certificates and within what period

cards.title: First morning at Sarawat Bank
cards.setting: Customer Care Department, Sarawat Bank head office, King Fahd Road, Riyadh. 8:30 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Sarawat Bank, a fictional conventional bank with branches from Tabuk to Jazan, as a Consumer Protection Officer in the Customer Care Department.
Welcome! I'm Noura Al-Qahtani, head of Customer Care. Your first file is already on the desk: a complaint from a retired teacher in Taif.
I am Saleh Al-Ghamdi. I asked your branch for a simple account update. I left with a credit card I never wanted, and now a collector calls me every evening.
Faisal Al-Harbi, branch manager in Jeddah. Our staff follow the procedures. The customer signed the form.
A signature is not the whole test. SAMA asks whether he was treated fairly, informed clearly and served by trained people.
Majed Al-Zahrani from Compliance. SAMA's consumer protection team may review our front-line training records next quarter.
Then we start at the Charter Hall: the principles every SAMA-supervised institution must live by. Ready?

scenes.heading: One instrument
scenes.narration: In August 2022 SAMA issued the Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules. They replaced the separate consumer protection principles SAMA had issued earlier for banks, insurers and finance companies.

scenes.heading: SAMA's power
scenes.narration: The rules rest on the Saudi Central Bank Law, which gives SAMA the task of protecting consumers of financial institutions, and on the Banking Control Law, which lets SAMA set the conditions banks must follow when dealing with customers.

scenes.heading: Who is protected
scenes.narration: A consumer here is a natural person who uses products and services of a SAMA-licensed institution. Employees include direct and outsourced staff.

scenes.heading: The purpose
scenes.narration: Three aims: keep pace with the international high-level principles, make sure consumers are treated with transparency, honesty and fairness, and let them reach good-quality services at reasonable cost.

scenes.heading: Enforcement
scenes.narration: SAMA can follow up on how the rules are applied and act on violations, including penalties, fines or orders to correct.

cards.title: How the document is built
cards.caption: The principles say what outcome customers must get; the rules say how the institution delivers it.

items.label: Section 1: purpose and definitions
items.detail: Who is a consumer, what counts as a complaint, documented channels, day and business day.

items.label: Section 2: ten principles
items.detail: The general framework every institution must observe in all dealings.

items.label: Section 3: general conduct rules
items.detail: Twenty-six rules for all institutions: disclosure, documents, data, training, complaints.

items.label: Section 4: specific conduct rules
items.detail: Rules for banks, finance companies, payment firms and card issuers.

items.label: Section 5: concluding provisions
items.detail: Minimum standard, SAMA follow-up and penalties, replacement of older principles.

cards.title: The ten principles in plain words
cards.prompt: Match each SAMA principle to what it expects of Sarawat Bank.

pairs.right: Fairness at every stage, with extra care for low-income, less educated, older and special-needs customers
Clear, current, accurate information on terms, fees, risks, rights and how to end the relationship
Professional service that protects the consumer's financial interests, with enough staff and channels
Mechanisms that protect personal and financial data, including Personal Data Protection Law rights
A clear, effective mechanism and fair resolution of each complaint without delay
The bank stays responsible when an outsourced provider deals with consumers

cards.question: A customer complains orally at the counter that a fee was 'unfair', and the fee was in fact correct. Under SAMA's definitions, is this a complaint?
options: No, because it was not made in writing
No, because the fee was charged correctly
Yes, any written or verbal expression of dissatisfaction is a complaint, justified or not
Only if the customer asks for a reference number
cards.explanation: SAMA defines a complaint as any written or verbal expression of dissatisfaction with a service, whether or not it is justified. It must be logged and handled even if the bank turns out to be right.

cards.back: Programmes that build consumers' knowledge and skills, explain major risks and help them make informed decisions.
Effective technical and control systems to limit and detect fraud, embezzlement or misuse, and action when it happens.
Consumers can easily search and compare products and providers; the institution keeps quality and innovation up.
A written conflict-of-interest policy and procedures that identify transactions likely to create a conflict.

cards.title: Rule 14 and Rule 15: people, training and monitoring
cards.body:
Two general conduct rules speak directly to staff:

- **Rule 14:** the institution must make sure **all employees** work efficiently and follow codes of conduct and ethics when serving current or potential consumers. It must **train front-line employees** who deal directly with consumers **on a regular basis** and make sure they obtain the **necessary professional certificates**, so they know how to deal with consumers, the products and services offered, and SAMA's relevant instructions.
- **Rule 15:** the institution must monitor front-line performance through **periodic or confidential visits** to branches, the call centre and **collection staff, including third-party employees**, and send **semi-annual reports** to senior management.

Remember the definition: 'employees' include outsourced staff. A contracted call-centre agent is in scope.

cards.title: SAMA's professional certificates for bank staff
cards.caption: Set out in SAMA circular 44029338 of October 2022, which builds on the 2019 circular on professional certificates.

items.label: Who
items.left: Front-line staff: customer care, call centre, branch staff and their managers
items.right: Staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals, plus branch managers

items.label: Third-party staff
items.left: Included if contracted through a third party
items.right: Included if contracted through a third party

items.label: Compliance rate
items.left: At least 90% of the target staff
items.right: At least 90% of the target staff

cards.title: The mystery shopper report
cards.setting: Sarawat Bank, Al-Rawdah branch, Jeddah. Two weeks later.

lines.text: Head office sent a confidential visit report. The visitor asked about a personal loan and our new teller could not explain the fees.
That is exactly what Rule 15 visits are for. How long has the teller been with us?
Five months. She came from a staffing agency, so HR never enrolled her for the certificate.
Agency staff count. The circular names people contracted through a third party.
Let's decide what to do before the next report goes to senior management.

cards.title: Closing the training gap
cards.situation: Faisal's branch has six front-line staff. Two agency tellers have no retail banking certificate; one joined five months ago, the other eleven months ago. The confidential visit found weak fee explanations. The semi-annual monitoring report is due next month.

choices.text: Enrol both agency tellers for the certificate now, give targeted fee training, and record the gap and the fix in the monitoring report.
choices.outcome: Best. Third-party front-line staff need the certificate within a year of employment, Rule 14 requires regular training, and Rule 15 expects the findings to reach senior management with action taken.

choices.text: Move the two tellers to back-office roles until the next intake, and say nothing in the report.
choices.outcome: Partly helpful for customers, but hiding a monitoring finding defeats Rule 15's purpose and does not build the skills the rules expect.

choices.text: Do nothing: agency staff are the agency's responsibility, not Sarawat Bank's.
choices.outcome: Poor. SAMA's definitions and the certificate circular include outsourced staff, and Principle 9 keeps the bank responsible for outsourced service.

choices.text: Ask the tellers to sign a statement that they read the fee schedule, and close the finding.
choices.outcome: Poor. A signature is not training or certification and would not fix the weak explanations the visit found.

cards.title: Who needs which certificate?
cards.prompt: Sort each Sarawat Bank role by the professional certificate SAMA's circular requires.

items.text: Call-centre agent answering account questions
Customer care department employee
Agency teller at a branch counter
Personal finance officer approving loans to individuals
Outsourced sales agent arranging credit for individuals
Branch manager

cards.question: Which staff does Rule 15 expressly mention for performance monitoring visits?
options: Only permanent branch tellers
Branches, the call centre and collection staff, including third-party employees
Only staff who received a complaint in the last year
Senior management and the board
cards.explanation: Rule 15 names branches, the call centre and collection staff, and expressly includes third-party employees. Results go to senior management in semi-annual reports.

cards.title: Real case: SAMA launches SAMACares (2020)
cards.body:
In 2020 SAMA, then still called the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority, announced the **SAMACares** mobile application for customers of banks, insurers, finance companies and payment companies, in Arabic and English.

- Customers could file, view and follow up complaints and answer requests from their institution.
- SAMA's message was clear: contact your bank first; if it does not cooperate, complain to SAMA's Consumer Protection Department through SAMACares or the toll-free number.
- SAMA stated it would impose penalties and take the measures the laws allow against violators.

SAMA later replaced the SAMACares system with a Complaint Management System by a July 2025 circular. The lesson for you is unchanged: the regulator sees complaints your bank fails to resolve, so fair first-line handling matters.

cards.title: Charter Hall take-aways
items: SAMA's Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules (August 2022) replaced earlier sector principles and protect natural-person consumers.
Ten principles set the outcomes: fairness, disclosure, education, ethics, fraud protection, privacy, complaints, competition, outsourcing, conflicts.
Rule 14: all staff follow conduct codes; front-line staff are trained regularly and hold the required professional certificates.
Rule 15: periodic or confidential visits to branches, call centre and collection staff (third-party included), with semi-annual reports.
Front-line and credit staff, including third-party staff, need SAMA's certificates within one year of employment, with at least 90% coverage.

cards.prompt: Think about your own role. Which of the ten principles do you apply most often, and when did you last receive training that covered SAMA's instructions for the products you discuss with customers?

quiz.question: Which SAMA instrument, issued in August 2022, sets the ten principles and the general and specific conduct rules for treating consumers?
options: The Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks
The Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions
The Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules
The Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures for creditors
quiz.explanation: The 2022 Financial Consumer Protection Principles and Rules contain the ten principles and the conduct rules. The other instruments deal with compliance, governance and collection.

quiz.question: Under SAMA's definitions, who is a 'consumer' for these principles and rules?
options: Any company or individual holding an account at the bank
Only customers who have taken out a financing product
Any person who has filed a complaint with SAMA
A natural person using a licensed institution's services
quiz.explanation: The rules define a consumer as a natural person who benefits from products and services of licensed institutions. Companies are not consumers under this definition, and the term is not limited to borrowers.

quiz.question: A call-centre agent employed by an outsourcing firm handles Sarawat Bank's card enquiries. How do the rules treat this agent?
options: As outside the rules, since only direct staff are covered
As covered only if the agent works on bank premises
As an employee, since the definition covers outsourced staff
As the outsourcing firm's concern alone, under its service contract
quiz.explanation: SAMA's definition of employees covers all staff, whether directly contracted or outsourced, and Principle 9 keeps the bank responsible for outsourced services.

quiz.question: Which principle requires special attention to low-income and less educated people, older people and those with special needs?
options: Principle 3, education and awareness
Principle 1, equitable and fair treatment
Principle 8, competition between providers
Principle 2, disclosure and transparency
quiz.explanation: Principle 1 requires fair and honest treatment at all stages and calls for due care and special attention to these groups. Education and disclosure principles support them but do not carry that wording.

quiz.question: What does Rule 14 require for front-line employees who deal directly with consumers?
options: Regular training and the necessary professional certificates
A single induction course when they are first hired
Annual sign-off on the product fee schedule by their line manager
A written exam set and marked by SAMA each year
quiz.explanation: Rule 14 requires front-line staff to be trained on a regular basis and to obtain the professional certificates needed for consumer skills, products and SAMA's instructions. A one-off induction is not enough.

quiz.question: How often must reports on the performance monitoring of front-line staff reach senior management under Rule 15?
options: Every six months
Every month
Once a year
Only when SAMA asks for them
quiz.explanation: Rule 15 requires semi-annual reports to senior management on the monitoring of front-line employees.

quiz.question: A branch hired a teller through an agency eleven months ago. She has no retail banking fundamentals certificate. What is the best assessment?
options: She is in scope and must certify within a year of starting
She is out of scope because she is employed by the agency, not the bank
She is in scope but has three years to certify
She needs only the credit adviser certificate
quiz.explanation: SAMA's circular covers front-line staff contracted through a third party and requires the certificate within one year of employment. She has about a month left.

quiz.question: Which staff group does SAMA's circular require to hold the credit adviser certificate, apart from those directly granting credit to individuals?
options: Call-centre agents
Branch managers
Internal auditors
Treasury dealers
quiz.explanation: The circular lists staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals and also branch managers. Call-centre agents need the retail banking fundamentals certificate instead.

quiz.question: Sarawat Bank's HR head says 82% of target front-line staff hold the retail banking certificate and 'that is close enough'. What does SAMA's circular expect?
options: A rate of at least 75%, so the bank is compliant
Full 100% coverage on the day staff start work
No set rate, as long as a training plan is approved by the board
A compliance rate of at least 90% of the staff concerned
quiz.explanation: The 2022 circular sets a compliance rate of no less than 90% for the employees concerned, with each person certified within a year of employment.

quiz.question: What can SAMA do when it finds that an institution has violated the consumer protection principles and rules?
options: Only issue a private warning letter to the chief executive
Impose penalties or fines, or require corrective action
Nothing, since the principles are guidance
Refer the matter to the consumer's employer
quiz.explanation: The concluding provisions let SAMA follow up on application of the rules and take the actions it deems appropriate, including penalties, fines or requests for corrective action.

sessions.title: Clear Disclosure, Fair Documents and Opening Accounts the SAMA Way
sessions.summary: Apply SAMA's general conduct rules on contracts, disclosure forms, fees, notices and documents, and the Account Opening Rules on deposits, timelines, customer presence, account information and staff training before tellers take up their posts.
objectives: Apply the disclosure and document rules: initial disclosure form, Arabic terms, minimum font size, no blank signatures
Explain notice periods and timelines: 30 days before changes, application messages, three working days for decisions, five working days for documents
Apply the Account Opening Rules on deposits, opening timelines, customer presence and the account information card
Explain why tellers and customer service staff must complete KYC, AML/CFT and ethics courses before taking up their posts

cards.title: The form with empty boxes
cards.setting: Sarawat Bank, Shihar branch, Taif. Monday morning.

lines.text: I came only to update my ID. The young man gave me three papers to sign and said he would fill in the rest later.
We were busy that day. Pre-signing saves the customer time at the counter.
Faisal, SAMA's rules say we must never ask for a signature on an empty or incomplete document. That is how a credit card appeared that he never chose.
And nobody gave me any copy. I only learned about the card from a text message.
Then this stage is the Counter of Clarity. Every document, every fee and every notice has a rule behind it.

scenes.heading: Read before signing
scenes.narration: Rule 1 asks the bank to encourage consumers to read contracts, the initial disclosure form and the terms, and to check that they understand them.

scenes.heading: One clear disclosure form
scenes.narration: Rule 5 requires an initial disclosure form in simple language, covering the product, how fees and commissions are calculated and the term cost, with the consumer's acknowledgement that they read and understood it.

scenes.heading: Readable terms
scenes.narration: Terms must be in simple Arabic, with an English copy on request, and contracts and annexes must use a font size of at least 14. Never ask for a signature on an empty or incomplete document.

scenes.heading: Messages that track the request
scenes.narration: Right after an application, the bank sends a text with the subject, reference number, expected date and toll-free number, and it reports acceptance or rejection within three working days, giving reasons and how to object.

scenes.heading: Copies straight away
scenes.narration: All product documents go to the consumer immediately, on paper or electronically as the consumer prefers, with an acknowledgement of receipt for paper copies.

cards.title: Clocks the rules set
cards.caption: Day means calendar day; working or business day excludes weekends and holidays.

items.label: Notice of a change in terms
items.detail: At least 30 days before it takes effect, by text message and other documented channels; the consumer may object.

items.label: Decision on an application
items.detail: Acceptance or rejection by text, with reasons and the objection route if rejected.

items.label: Copies of forms, terms and contracts
items.detail: Provided on the consumer's request.

items.label: Refunds from a technical error
items.detail: Returned to every affected consumer without waiting for claims.

items.label: Amortisation schedule for a borrower
items.detail: Free of charge on request, once, for default or early payment.

cards.question: Sarawat Bank plans to change a card product's terms, which the agreement allows. What must it do first?
options: Post the new terms on the website on the day they take effect
Tell the consumer by text and other documented channels at least 30 days ahead and let them object
Tell the consumer at the next branch visit
Ask SAMA to approve the change for each customer
cards.explanation: Rule 4 requires notice by text message to the registered mobile number and other documented channels at least 30 days before the change, and a way for the consumer to object.

cards.title: Allowed or not allowed?
cards.prompt: Sort each practice under SAMA's general conduct rules.

items.text: Giving an English copy of the terms when the customer asks
Displaying the fee list in the branch and on the website
Asking the customer to sign a blank form 'to save time'
Raising a contract's fees after signing because costs rose
Printing contract annexes in 10-point type to fit one page
Sending the contract by email because the customer prefers it
Keeping a technical-error refund until the customer claims it
Stating the purpose of an OTP in the text message

cards.title: Fees, data and channels in the general rules
cards.body:
Several general conduct rules apply at every counter and call:

- **Fees:** no increase in fees and commissions after the contract is signed (third-party charges tied to the financed asset are the narrow exception, and only if disclosed at signing). The fee list, including third-party fees, is displayed in branches and published online.
- **Confidentiality (Rule 11):** the bank protects consumer information wherever it is held. Permanent, temporary and third-party staff sign a **consumer information confidentiality form**, and access is limited to authorised people.
- **Secure channels (Rule 12):** if consumers suffer direct loss because a channel was penetrated or weakly secured, they are compensated. OTP messages must state their purpose.
- **No discrimination (Rule 24):** no biased treatment based on race, gender, religion, colour, age, disability, marital status or any other ground.
- **Hardship (Rule 23):** consider humanitarian cases and find suitable solutions before legal action.

cards.title: A new branch, a new rulebook
cards.setting: Sarawat Bank, Al-Rawdah branch, Jeddah. Account opening desk.

lines.text: A young engineer wants a current account. My teller asked for a SAR 3,000 opening deposit, as usual.
That 'usual' is a problem. SAMA's Account Opening Rules say the bank must not require any deposit to open an account.
And if he never deposits?
If nothing is deposited within 90 days, the bank closes the account. Also, the teller you hired last week: has she done the KYC, AML/CFT and ethics courses?
She starts the course next month.
Then she cannot sit at that desk yet. Rule 9 is clear.

cards.title: Opening an account for a resident individual
cards.caption: Based on SAMA's Account Opening Rules (2019 and later amendments).

items.label: Customer present
items.detail: As a basic rule, a new customer is present, unless a power of attorney expressly allows opening accounts.

items.label: ID checked and copied
items.detail: Copies compared with originals, stamped and signed; no transaction before the ID is examined.

items.label: KYC and risk
items.detail: Understand the customer and their activity and assess the risk before or during opening.

items.label: No deposit demanded
items.detail: No minimum deposit as a condition; unfunded accounts close after 90 days.

items.label: Open on time
items.detail: Within one business day, or two if internal approvals are needed; tell the customer in writing what is missing.

items.label: Account information card
items.detail: Give the customer's name, account number and IBAN as evidence of opening.

cards.title: The teller who is not ready yet
cards.situation: Faisal is short-staffed during the end-of-month salary rush. A new teller joined last week and has not yet attended the KYC, AML/CFT and banker ethics courses. Faisal wants her on the counter tomorrow.

choices.text: Keep her off the teller and customer service posts until she finishes the courses, and borrow a trained teller from a nearby branch for the rush.
choices.outcome: Best. Rule 9 of the Account Opening Rules says banks must not assign tellers or customer service staff before they attend these courses.

choices.text: Let her serve customers but only for cash deposits, which carry less risk.
choices.outcome: Still a teller assignment. The rule does not have a low-risk exception, and deposits are a classic AML exposure.

choices.text: Seat her next to an experienced teller who approves each transaction, and fast-track her course to this week.
choices.outcome: Better supervision and a faster course help, but she is still being assigned to the post before training. Acceptable only as observation, not serving.

choices.text: Let her work and ask her to read the AML policy tonight.
choices.outcome: Poor. Reading a policy is not attending the required courses, and continuing training must also cover the rules in depth.

cards.title: Account opening rules in practice
cards.prompt: Match each situation to the rule that applies.

pairs.left: Customer applies with complete documents, no approvals needed
pairs.right: Open the account within one business day

pairs.left: Customer cannot visit for reasons beyond their control
pairs.right: Two or more staff with different powers may visit to collect information
Allowed, all under one customer information file number
Give priority and care so banking services are easy to obtain
Tell the applicant in writing what is missing or extra

cards.front: Can the bank refuse to open the account?
cards.back: No. The bank must open an account for a blind or illiterate customer who asks, and offer an ATM card and a chequebook on request.
A personal reference aged 15 or over who can read to the customer and witness, or a customer service representative.
A branch or operations manager certifies that terms and controls were read out and explained.
A thumbprint and personal stamp; a handwritten signature is allowed if the customer chooses it, and that choice is documented.

cards.question: A customer says she was told to deposit SAR 1,000 before her account could be opened. What does SAMA's rule say?
options: The bank may set any minimum deposit it publishes
The bank must not require a deposit; an account with no deposit within 90 days is closed
Only salary accounts may be opened without a deposit
A deposit is needed only for non-Saudi residents
cards.explanation: The Account Opening Rules forbid a deposit as a condition of opening. If no amount is deposited within 90 days, the bank must close the account.

cards.title: Common mistakes at the counter
cards.body:
- Saying 'sign here, I'll complete it later'. Never: empty or incomplete documents cannot be signed.
- Giving documents 'next week'. Provide them at once, in the format the customer prefers.
- Quoting fees from memory. Use the published fee list and the initial disclosure form.
- Explaining a rejection with 'system decision'. The text message must give the reason and the objection route.
- Letting new tellers serve before their KYC, AML/CFT and ethics courses.

cards.title: Counter of Clarity take-aways
items: Initial disclosure form in simple language, acknowledged by the customer; terms in Arabic (English on request); font 14 or larger.
No signature on empty or incomplete documents; documents handed over immediately in the customer's preferred format.
30 days' notice of term changes, text messages on applications, decisions within 3 working days, copies within 5 working days.
No fee increases after signing; refunds from technical errors within 5 working days without a claim.
Accounts: no deposit condition, opening within 1 or 2 business days, account information card, and trained tellers only.

cards.prompt: Look at one form or message your team gives customers. Would a first-time customer understand the fees, the risks and how to object? What would you change?

quiz.question: What is the minimum font size SAMA requires for contracts, annexes and disclosure forms?
quiz.explanation: Rule 6 requires a standard, readable font of at least size 14 in contracts and annexes, including disclosure forms and terms.

quiz.question: In which language must terms and conditions be drafted under Rule 3?
options: English, with an Arabic summary
Either language, as the bank chooses
Both languages printed side by side
Arabic, with an English copy on request
quiz.explanation: Terms must be drafted in simple, clear Arabic, and an English copy must be provided if the consumer asks for it.

quiz.question: A customer applies for a personal loan online. Within how long must the bank tell her by text whether it is accepted or rejected?
options: Five working days at most
One business day at most
Ten calendar days at most
Three working days at most
quiz.explanation: Rule 10 requires a text notification of acceptance or rejection within a maximum of three working days, with reasons and the objection route if rejected.

quiz.question: A system fault charged 2,000 customers twice for a transfer fee. What must the bank do with the extra fees?
options: Return them only to customers who complain about the charge
Return them within five working days without waiting for claims
Keep them until month-end reconciliation is complete
Return them within thirty days, together with a written apology letter
quiz.explanation: Rule 13 forbids the bank from benefiting from refunds caused by technical errors; they go back to each affected consumer within five working days without waiting for claims.

quiz.question: A customer asks for a copy of his loan contract and the collateral documents. What is the deadline?
options: Two working days
Ten working days
Five working days
Thirty calendar days
quiz.explanation: Rule 21 requires copies of original forms, updated terms, contracts and collateral documents, and insurance policies within five working days of the request.

quiz.question: A teller asks a customer to sign a blank transfer form so she can fill in the beneficiary later. Which statement is right?
options: It breaches the rule against signing incomplete documents
It is fine if the customer gives verbal consent
It is acceptable if the branch manager countersigns the form afterwards
It breaches only the bank's internal policy
quiz.explanation: Rule 6 says the institution must not request the consumer's signature of any type on an empty or incomplete document, and must protect consumers' documents and signatures.

quiz.question: Under the Account Opening Rules, how quickly must a bank open an account for an individual who meets all requirements and needs no internal approvals?
options: Within one business day
Within two business days
Within five business days
On the same calendar day
quiz.explanation: The rule sets one business day where no approvals are needed and two business days where the bank's departments must approve.

quiz.question: What happens to a new account if the customer deposits nothing in it within 90 days?
options: The bank may charge a dormancy fee
The bank must close it
It becomes an inoperative account
The bank must report it to SAMA
quiz.explanation: Banks may not demand a deposit to open an account, but an account with no deposit within 90 days must be closed (government and enforcement court accounts have exceptions).

quiz.question: Which courses must a teller or customer service employee attend before the bank assigns them to that post, under Rule 9 of the Account Opening Rules?
options: Sales techniques, product pricing and cross-selling
KYC, AML/CFT measures, and banker ethics and conduct
Cyber security, business continuity and outsourcing
Credit analysis, collateral and debt collection
quiz.explanation: Rule 9 bars assigning tellers or customer service staff before they attend KYC, AML/CFT and professional ethics courses, and requires continuing on-the-job training on the rules.

quiz.question: A blind customer wants to open an account and has no one with her. How should the branch proceed under the Account Opening Rules?
options: Decline the request until she returns with a personal reference aged 15 or over
Open it only as a joint account with a relative
Staff explain the terms; a branch or operations manager certifies it
Open it but refuse an ATM card for safety reasons
quiz.explanation: Without a personal reference, a customer service representative explains the procedures and terms, certified by an authorised signatory such as the branch or operations manager. Refusal or limits on cards are not allowed.

sessions.title: Complaints, Vulnerable Customers and Persons with Disabilities
sessions.summary: Handle complaints the way SAMA expects: channels, reference numbers, timelines, records, escalation and the Customer Care Department. Serve vulnerable customers and persons with disabilities fairly under the consumer protection principles and SAMA's instructions for persons with disabilities.
objectives: Describe the complaint mechanism required by the general conduct rules: channels, display, reference numbers, records and escalation
Explain the role, units and complaint-handling timeline of a bank's Customer Care Department
Apply SAMA's instructions for services to persons with disabilities, including the guide and trained specialised staff
Recognise vulnerable customers and the care, non-discrimination and hardship duties that protect them

cards.title: Mr Saleh calls again
cards.setting: Customer Care Department, Sarawat Bank, Riyadh. Tuesday, 10:15 am.

lines.text: I complained at the Taif branch two weeks ago. Nobody gave me a number and nobody called back.
Mr Saleh, I'm sorry. I'll log it now. You will receive a text with your reference number and the handling period.
And my wife uses a wheelchair. The branch ramp is blocked by a planter and the kiosk is too high for her.
Two problems, two sets of rules. Thank you for telling me both.
Noura, the Taif staff thought a verbal complaint at the counter was just a chat.
Written or verbal, justified or not: it's a complaint. Welcome to the Listening Desk.

cards.title: What a complaint mechanism must include

scenes.heading: Many doors in
scenes.narration: The bank offers several channels for complaints, inquiries and requests: at least a toll-free number, branches or the website, smartphone apps and email.

scenes.heading: Visible process
scenes.narration: The complaint handling mechanism is displayed in the head office and branches and published on the website and apps.

scenes.heading: A number and a deadline
scenes.narration: Receipt is documented and the consumer gets a text with the main reference number and the handling period, plus contact details for follow-up.

scenes.heading: Records kept
scenes.narration: The channel used with the consumer is documented and the records are kept for at least five years.

scenes.heading: Escalation
scenes.narration: If the consumer is unhappy with the result, the bank explains how to escalate within the bank or directs them to the competent authority, as they prefer.

cards.title: The complaint loop
cards.caption: Rule 20 adds performance indicators for directly filed complaints, reported quarterly to the highest executive.

items.label: Receive and log
items.detail: Any channel, any form; text with reference number and period.

items.label: Investigate and resolve
items.detail: Fairly and effectively, within the period SAMA sets.

items.label: Respond with evidence
items.detail: Detailed result and supporting documents through a documented channel.

items.label: Escalate if unhappy
items.detail: Higher level in the bank or the competent authority.

items.label: Measure and fix causes
items.detail: Satisfaction and quality indicators; root causes addressed.

cards.question: How long must a bank keep the record of the channel it used to communicate with a complaining consumer?
options: One year
At least five years
Until the complaint is closed
Ten years in every case
cards.explanation: Rule 19 requires the bank to document the communication channel and keep the records for at least five years.

cards.title: SAMA's Customer Care Department rules for banks (2023)
cards.caption: From SAMA's Regulations for Establishing Customer Care Departments in Banks, effective July 2023.

items.label: Complaint handling period
items.detail: Maximum time for the complaints unit to handle a complaint from receipt.

items.label: Satisfaction target
items.detail: Minimum share of complaints the customer rates as satisfactory; SAMA may adjust it.

items.label: SLA compliance target
items.detail: Minimum indicator for handling complaints within the regulatory period.

items.label: Manager's settlement authority
items.detail: Department manager or delegate may resolve complaints up to this amount.

cards.title: Inside the Customer Care Department
cards.body:
SAMA's 2023 regulations require every bank to set up a Customer Care Department by **board decision**, reporting **directly to the highest executive** and not linked to any other department. SAMA's written approval is needed before a manager is appointed.

It has at least **three units**:

- **Complaints Handling:** multiple channels, an electronic system that tracks each complaint, a reference number and period by text, and handling within **five working days**.
- **Quality and Performance Analysis:** checks handling quality, analyses root causes, and reports monthly to the CEO and quarterly to senior management and the board.
- **Financial Awareness and Education:** annual awareness plans; its staff may **not** contact customers to market products.

Department staff need the **retail banking** and **credit adviser** certificates and training at least **once a year**. The department is audited annually by Internal Audit and Compliance and holds ISO 10002 certification, renewed annually.

cards.title: Handling Mr Saleh's complaint
cards.prompt: Put the steps in the order SAMA's rules expect.
steps: Record the complaint, whatever the channel, as soon as it is received
Send a text with the reference number and the handling period
Investigate with the branch and the card team within the set period
Give the customer the detailed result with supporting documents
Explain escalation within the bank or to the competent authority if he is not satisfied
Feed the case into root-cause analysis and the satisfaction indicators

cards.title: The ramp and the kiosk
cards.setting: Sarawat Bank, Shihar branch, Taif. The next afternoon.

lines.text: The planter is gone and the ramp is clear. But the accessible kiosk on our list was never installed here.
SAMA's instructions for persons with disabilities cover the built environment: ramps, parking, kiosks at the right height, equipped offices.
My wife also asked a teller to read the card terms to her. He said he was too busy.
The bank must assign an employee to read the main terms to blind and visually impaired customers and help with forms if asked.
Do my staff even have the guide?
The instructions require one, and specialised staff trained to use it. Let's check who in Taif is trained.

cards.title: SAMA's instructions for persons with disabilities (2020)

cards.back: Each institution sets up an administrative unit to make sure policies and services meet the needs of persons with disabilities.
Ramps, accessible exits, reserved parking, suitable kiosks and equipped offices; mobile services for severe disabilities where possible.
Allowed through medical reports or supporting documents, but only once.
Contracts in accessible formats such as Braille; an employee reads main terms and helps fill in forms on request.
No refusal or restriction of a financial service because of disability without a legal basis.
A service guide, and specialised staff trained and qualified to serve persons with disabilities easily.

cards.title: A customer with a hearing impairment
cards.situation: A customer with a hearing impairment visits the Jeddah branch to dispute a card charge. The teller struggles to communicate and suggests he 'come back with someone who can talk for him'. The customer leaves upset and writes a complaint on the branch tablet.

choices.text: Log the complaint, arrange a trained specialised staff member or suitable communication aid, and give him priority service to resolve the dispute.
choices.outcome: Best. The instructions require trained specialised staff, suitable means of explanation and high priority, and the complaint must be logged and handled.

choices.text: Apologise and ask him to use the mobile app instead.
choices.outcome: Partly helpful, but it pushes him away from the branch and ignores the duty to serve him there and to log his complaint.

choices.text: Ask him to bring a medical report proving the disability before serving him.
choices.outcome: Poor. Verification may happen only once and must not become a barrier; it is not needed to handle a card dispute.

choices.text: Tell him the card dispute must be handled by phone only.
choices.outcome: Poor. Phone-only handling excludes him because of his disability, which the instructions forbid without a legal basis.

cards.title: Fair or unfair treatment?
cards.prompt: Sort each practice by SAMA's principles and instructions.

items.text: Explaining a product slowly to an older customer and checking understanding
Refusing a credit card because the applicant is a widow
Giving priority service to a customer using a wheelchair
Asking for proof of disability at every visit
Offering contract terms in Braille to a blind customer
Starting legal action at once against a customer in sudden hardship
Sending a less educated customer the disclosure form with a verbal walk-through

cards.question: Which rule asks the bank to consider humanitarian cases and find suitable solutions before taking legal action against consumers in sudden financial difficulty?
options: Rule 23 of the general conduct rules
Rule 9 of the specific conduct rules
Principle 8 on competition
Rule 1 of the general conduct rules
cards.explanation: Rule 23 requires the institution to take humanitarian cases and its social responsibility into account and to look for suitable solutions before legal action.

cards.title: Words that turn a complaint into a fix
cards.body:
- Never say 'that's not a complaint'. Log it and give the reference number.
- Ask how the customer prefers to be contacted, and use a documented channel.
- Promise only the period the system sends; don't guess.
- If a customer has a disability, ask what support helps, then provide it without making them prove it again.
- Tell unhappy customers how to escalate. Sending them on is not a failure; it is a right.

cards.title: Listening Desk take-aways
items: A complaint is any written or verbal expression of dissatisfaction, justified or not.
Multiple channels, a visible mechanism, a text with the reference number and period, records for at least five years, and an escalation route.
Banks' Customer Care Departments report to the top executive, handle complaints within five working days and train staff at least yearly.
Persons with disabilities: accessible premises and contracts, help reading terms, no exclusion, a service guide and trained specialised staff.
Principle 1 and Rules 23 and 24 protect vulnerable customers: special care, hardship solutions and no discrimination.

cards.prompt: Picture a customer with a visual, hearing or mobility impairment arriving at your workplace today. What would they meet first, and who on your team is trained to serve them?

quiz.question: Which channels must at a minimum be available for complaints under Rule 17?
options: Branches only, with a written complaint form
A postal address and a fax number
Toll-free number, branches or website, smartphone apps and email
The SAMA website and a written letter to the bank's head office only
quiz.explanation: Rule 17 requires multiple channels including at minimum a toll-free number, branches and/or website, smartphone applications and email.

quiz.question: A customer files a complaint by phone. What must he receive by text message to his registered mobile number?
options: A link to SAMA's complaint portal only
A satisfaction survey before any investigation
The main reference number and the handling period
The name of the branch manager responsible
quiz.explanation: Rule 19 requires the bank to document receipt and send the reference number and specified handling period by text message.

quiz.question: Within what maximum period must a bank's complaints unit handle a complaint under SAMA's Customer Care Department regulations?
options: Ten working days from receipt
Five working days from receipt
Fifteen calendar days from receipt
Thirty calendar days from receipt
quiz.explanation: The 2023 regulations require the complaints handling unit to handle complaints within a maximum of five working days from receipt.

quiz.question: To whom does a bank's Customer Care Department report under SAMA's 2023 regulations?
options: Directly to the highest executive position in the bank
To the head of retail banking
To the chief compliance officer
To the board's audit committee through the chief internal auditor
quiz.explanation: The department is set up by board decision and reports directly to the CEO, general manager or managing director, and must not be linked to any other department.

quiz.question: A customer is unhappy with the bank's final response to his complaint. What must the bank do under Rule 19?
options: Explain escalation in the bank or to the competent authority
Close the file, because the bank has already sent its final reply in writing
Reopen the complaint only if he pays a review fee
Ask him to restart the complaint through a branch
quiz.explanation: Rule 19(g) requires the bank to provide the escalation route to a higher level in the bank or to the competent authority, as the consumer prefers.

quiz.question: How often may a financial institution verify that a customer has a disability under SAMA's instructions?
options: Every year
Only once
At every branch visit
Whenever a new product is opened
quiz.explanation: The instructions allow verification through medical reports or supporting documents, provided it takes place only once.

quiz.question: Which duty in SAMA's instructions for persons with disabilities is directly about staff training?
options: Preparing a service guide and training specialised staff to serve them
Installing ramps and reserving parking at every branch
Updating marketing policies to include disabled customers
Setting up an administrative unit for customers with disabilities at head office
quiz.explanation: Section III, paragraph 8(b) requires a guide on serving persons with disabilities and the training and qualification of specialised staff. The other duties are real but are not about training.

quiz.question: A blind customer asks for the main terms of a loan contract to be read to her. What do SAMA's instructions require?
options: She must bring a relative to read them
An assigned employee reads the main terms to her
She must sign a waiver of the reading
The bank emails the terms for later reading
quiz.explanation: The instructions require the institution to assign an employee to read the main terms and conditions to blind and visually impaired customers, and to help fill in forms if asked.

quiz.question: Which grounds of discrimination does Rule 24 expressly list?
options: Income, education level, nationality, occupation and place of residence only
Credit score, employer and length of relationship
Only gender and disability, as protected classes
Race, gender, religion, colour, age, disability, marital status
quiz.explanation: Rule 24 lists race, gender, religion, colour, age, disability and marital status, and adds 'any other forms of discrimination'.

quiz.question: Staff of the Financial Awareness and Education Unit want to call customers to promote a new savings account. What do SAMA's regulations say?
options: They may do so if the call includes an awareness message
They may do so only for low-risk savings products
They may do so with the department manager's approval
They may not contact customers to market products
quiz.explanation: The 2023 regulations prohibit employees of the awareness unit from contacting customers for marketing purposes, keeping education separate from sales.

sessions.title: Fair Collection under SAMA's 2025 Debt Collection Regulations
sessions.summary: Collect debts the way SAMA's March 2025 Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures require: who may be contacted and how often, which channels, objections, deduction limits, rescheduling, default management under Article 10, death and total disability, and proof that collection staff know the policy.
objectives: Apply the communication rules: who may be called, how often, when, and what must be recorded and kept
Handle objections and complaints during collection without breaching the regulations
Apply the limits on deductions, account blocking, late penalties and the rescheduling duties
Explain Article 10: due diligence before legal action, the board-approved collection policy and proof of staff and third-party awareness

cards.title: Evening calls
cards.setting: Collections Department, Sarawat Bank, Dammam. 4:00 pm.

lines.text: Reem Al-Otaibi, collections. I've read Mr Saleh's file. Our agency called him on the card he never wanted, sometimes at 9 pm.
They also called my son and my neighbour. And a man came to my house asking for money.
Mr Saleh, that should never happen. We've frozen collection on the card while your complaint is open.
The agency says our old policy allowed home visits 'in exceptional cases'.
The 2025 regulations replaced that. No visits to home or workplace under any circumstances.
Let's cross the Collection Bridge properly this time.

scenes.heading: New rules
scenes.narration: SAMA issued the Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures in March 2025. They replace the first edition for individual consumers and apply to banks, finance companies and the third parties that collect for them.

scenes.heading: Their aims
scenes.narration: Better collection with less default, professional conduct, minimum steps for contact and rescheduling, and protection of the privacy of consumers and guarantors.

scenes.heading: Who is covered
scenes.narration: Collection from the consumer, a natural person who obtained the financing, or the guarantor if the consumer defaults. Employees include staff contracted through a third party.

scenes.heading: Who answers
scenes.narration: The creditor is responsible for any violation committed by its employees or third parties, so the bank cannot blame its agency.

scenes.heading: Annual check
scenes.narration: The department that manages collection is reviewed and audited every year by Internal Audit and Compliance.

cards.title: Contact rules: do and don't
cards.caption: Article 4 of the 2025 regulations. Arabic is the main language, except for non-Arabic speakers.

items.label: Who
items.left: Call only the consumer or guarantor, and verify identity first
items.right: Call relatives, neighbours, colleagues or employers

items.label: How often
items.left: No more than 10 call attempts per 30 days per financing product

items.label: When
items.left: During official working hours, with a number the consumer can call back

items.label: Records
items.left: Tell the caller it is recorded; keep records for at least 10 years

items.label: Visits
items.right: Visit the home or workplace, under any circumstances

items.label: Letters
items.left: Plain envelopes with clear, legible content
items.right: Envelopes that show they contain debt collection material

cards.question: An agency collector wants to call a borrower with one personal loan for the eleventh time this month. What do the regulations say?
options: Allowed, if the borrower has missed three payments
Not allowed: the limit is ten call attempts per thirty days per financing product
Allowed, if the calls are made during working hours
Not allowed: only five calls a month are permitted
cards.explanation: Article 4 limits phone call attempts to the consumer or guarantor to ten at most every thirty days for each financing product.

cards.title: Collection channels and information
cards.prompt: Match each Article 5 requirement to its detail.

pairs.right: Email, registered mail, text, phone, the creditor's app or website, judicial notice
Creditor and collection department, or the third party and the creditor it acts for
The employee gives their name
The department's or third party's number and working hours
Easy to understand and clearly legible, headers and footers included

cards.title: Objections, deductions and limits
Lost job, lost sleep
cards.setting: Sarawat Bank, Dammam. Collections call review.

lines.text: A customer, Mr Turki, lost his job when his company closed. He's asking to reschedule his personal loan.
A compulsory change in circumstances, such as job loss, means we must offer rescheduling without new finance, extra fees or a change in the term cost.
Our sales team suggested a top-up loan to clear the arrears.
That is exactly the kind of solution the collection policy must avoid: it adds to his burden.
And the deadline once he gives us his documents?
Twenty working days at most, and we postpone his instalments until it's done.

cards.title: Mr Turki's rescheduling
cards.situation: Mr Turki has a personal loan with Sarawat Bank. His employer closed and he lost his job. He has sent the documents proving it and asked to reschedule. His next instalment falls due in five days.

choices.text: Offer rescheduling with no new finance, fees or term-cost change, complete it within 20 working days, and postpone deductions until it is done.
choices.outcome: Best. Article 9 requires this for a compulsory change in circumstances such as job loss.

choices.text: Offer a top-up loan to clear the arrears and lower the monthly payment.
choices.outcome: Poor. New finance increases his burden; the regulations require rescheduling without new finance, and the policy must avoid such solutions.

choices.text: Reschedule, but add an administration fee and take the next instalment as normal.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Rescheduling is offered, but the fee is not allowed and deductions must be postponed until it is complete.

choices.text: Tell him to wait until he has missed three payments, when the account formally defaults.
choices.outcome: Poor. Article 9 asks creditors to act proactively when signs of a change in credit status appear, before default.

cards.title: Article 10: managing default before going to the authorities
cards.caption: Article 10(1-3)(e): collection staff of the creditor and of third parties must know the policy and the creditor must be able to prove it.

items.label: Professional standards
items.detail: Staff give correct, complete information on status, procedures and possible legal action.

items.label: Internal procedures and SLAs
items.detail: Escalation so objections and complaints are resolved within SAMA's periods, measured electronically.

items.label: Written collection policy
items.detail: Approved by the board or the manager, as appropriate.

items.label: Fair solutions
items.detail: Settlement, rescheduling or deferral based on creditworthiness; avoid extra finance.

items.label: Clear information and complaint analysis
items.detail: Explain options and consequences; analyse complaint patterns and causes.

items.label: Review and awareness
items.detail: Review the policy at least every two years; staff and third parties aware of it, with proof.

cards.title: Proving collection staff know the policy
cards.prompt: Put Sarawat Bank's awareness steps in a sensible order.
steps: Board approves the written collection policy
Collections and agency staff receive training on the policy
Each collector completes a short test and signs an acknowledgement
Records of training, tests and acknowledgements are kept for every collector
Call monitoring and complaint analysis check the policy is followed
Policy and training are reviewed within two years or sooner if rules change

cards.title: Death, total disability and other protections

cards.back: Creditors exempt the consumer and guarantor from amounts due under the contract, as the contract provides, without waiting for an insurer's approval.
Within thirty days of receiving the death certificate or disability report, refunding amounts deducted after the event.
Only those listed in Article 11, such as contracts before 1 October 2018, self-harm or natural disasters, and only if the parties agreed to include them.
Among other tests, no full or partial payment for three consecutive months.
Deduction limits agreed with each joint consumer are respected.

cards.title: Real case: SAMA fines 16 institutions over responsible finance (2019)
cards.body:
In May 2019 SAMA announced fines on **16 financial institutions**, a mix of banks and finance companies, for breaching its principles of responsible finance for individuals. SAMA's statement pointed in particular to the **share of a borrower's total monthly income** taken up by repayments. It told the institutions to correct the violations and called on all supervised institutions to comply in a way that does not harm customers' rights and interests.

Why it matters for collection: the 2025 regulations make the creditor responsible for assessing affordability throughout the contract, and require rescheduling without new finance or fees when default stems from the creditor's own failure to assess creditworthiness, for example exceeding the statutory deduction ratios.

cards.question: Under Article 6, what must a collector do while a consumer's objection to the claimed amount is being resolved?
options: Continue reminders but reduce them to once a week
Stop contacting the consumer about the default until the complaint is resolved
Pass the account to an external agency
Report the consumer to the credit bureau immediately
cards.explanation: Article 6 forbids reminding the consumer or guarantor of defaults until the complaint is resolved, and requires a resolution time within SAMA's periods.

cards.title: Collection Bridge take-aways
items: Call only the consumer or guarantor, verify identity, stay within 10 attempts per 30 days per product and working hours, and never visit home or work.
Record calls, tell the consumer, and keep records for at least 10 years.
Pause default reminders while an objection is resolved; no deductions or blocking without court order, consent or contract terms.
Job loss and other compulsory changes mean rescheduling within 20 working days with no new finance, fees or term-cost change.
Article 10: board-approved policy, reviewed at least every two years, and proof that bank and agency collectors know it.

cards.prompt: If your bank or an agency acting for it called a member of your family about a debt, which of these rules would you most want them to follow, and how would you know they had been trained?

quiz.question: To whom do SAMA's 2025 Debt Collection Regulations and Procedures apply?
options: Only banks, and only for credit card debts
Only licensed collection agencies
Banks, finance companies and third parties collecting for them
All creditors in the Kingdom, including private individuals and employers
quiz.explanation: The regulations apply to creditors (banks and SAMA-supervised finance companies) and to third parties that carry out collection for them.

quiz.question: A collector calls a borrower's brother to ask him to remind the borrower to pay. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, if the brother is listed as an emergency contact
No, calls may go only to the consumer or guarantor
Yes, if the call is made during working hours
No, unless the borrower has been in default for a year
quiz.explanation: Article 4 forbids phone calls to anyone other than the consumer or guarantor and requires identity checks at the start of each call.

quiz.question: How long must creditors keep records of communications with consumers and guarantors?
options: At least ten years from the date of communication
At least five years from the date of communication
Until the debt has been fully repaid
Two years after the account is closed
quiz.explanation: Article 4 requires communications to be documented and kept for no less than ten years, and the consumer told at the start of a call that it is recorded.

quiz.question: When may a collector visit a defaulting consumer at home under the 2025 regulations?
options: Only after three unanswered calls
Never: home and workplace visits are banned
Only with a branch manager present
Only during official working hours
quiz.explanation: Article 4 forbids visiting the consumer or guarantor under any circumstances, whether at home or at work.

quiz.question: A borrower objects to the amount claimed. What may the collector NOT do until the objection is resolved?
options: Record the objection in the borrower's file
Contact the borrower with reminders of the default
Tell the borrower the expected resolution time
Register the complaint under SAMA's instructions
quiz.explanation: Article 6 requires recording and registering the objection and giving a time frame, and forbids default reminders until the complaint is resolved.

quiz.question: What is the maximum total of delay penalties or collection fees a creditor may charge over the whole finance period?
options: Two instalments' value
One percent of the finance amount
The value of one instalment
There is no limit if the contract allows it
quiz.explanation: Article 8 prohibits delay penalties or collection fees exceeding the due amount, with a maximum of one instalment's value for the entire finance period.

quiz.question: Within how many working days must a creditor complete a requested rescheduling after receiving the consumer's documents, for a compulsory change in circumstances?
options: Five working days
Ten working days
Thirty working days
Twenty working days
quiz.explanation: Article 9 requires rescheduling within a period not exceeding 20 working days from receipt of the necessary documents, with deductions postponed meanwhile.

quiz.question: Which solution should a board-approved collection policy avoid under Article 10?
options: Granting additional finance that raises the consumer's burden
Settling the debt by agreement between the two parties
Rescheduling the debt to suit the consumer's current means and income
Deferring instalments while the consumer recovers
quiz.explanation: Article 10(1-3)(a) lists settlement, rescheduling and deferral as possible solutions and says to avoid financing solutions, such as additional finance, that increase the burden.

quiz.question: Sarawat Bank uses an outside agency for card collections. What must the bank be able to show under Article 10?
options: That the agency holds its own collection licence
That agency staff all hold the credit adviser certificate from the institute
That the agency's policy was approved by SAMA
That bank and agency collectors know the policy, with proof
quiz.explanation: Article 10(1-3)(e) requires the creditor to ensure its own and third-party collection staff are aware of the policy and provide proof of that awareness.

quiz.question: How often, at most, must the written collection policy be reviewed and updated?
options: Every two years at most, or sooner when needed
Every five years at most
Only when SAMA issues new or amended collection rules
Every year, without exception
quiz.explanation: Article 10(1-3)(d) requires periodic review in line with best practice and the rules, updating as needed or every two years at most.

sessions.title: Conduct, Confidentiality, Staff Awareness Measures and Inspection Readiness
sessions.summary: Bring it together: SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics, customer data confidentiality, the control and awareness measures for branch and customer service staff (campaigns every three months, tests every six months, declarations on joining and yearly), the publication of SAMA penalties, and the evidence a SAMA review will ask for.
objectives: Apply SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics on signing, gifts, conflicts, confidentiality and reporting
Protect customer information using the need-to-know controls and staff duties SAMA sets
Explain the awareness measures for branch and customer service staff: three-monthly campaigns, six-monthly tests and declarations
Assemble the training, monitoring and audit evidence that shows compliance with SAMA's consumer protection instructions

cards.title: The balance on the screen
cards.setting: Sarawat Bank, Al-Rawdah branch, Jeddah. A quiet afternoon.

lines.text: A customer says his cousin, who works at our branch, told the family about his account balance at a wedding.
Did the cousin's job need access to that balance?
No. He works on cheque clearing. The screen just shows everything.
Then two rules failed: need-to-know access and the duty of confidentiality every employee signs.
And SAMA will ask when the branch last ran its confidentiality awareness campaign and staff test.
Final stage: the Vault of Trust. Let's get ready for the review.

cards.title: SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics (2019)

scenes.heading: Who they cover
scenes.narration: Board and committee members, executives, regular and contract staff, consultants and third-party employees of SAMA-supervised institutions.

scenes.heading: Read and signed
scenes.narration: The board adopts a conduct policy based on the principles. Managers make sure each employee reads and signs them and that the copy goes into the employee file. The institution explains them on joining.

scenes.heading: Stakeholders
scenes.narration: Clear, honest advice, accurate information, and immediate, fair handling of complaints and feedback.

scenes.heading: Corruption
scenes.narration: Staff must fight money laundering, bribery and favouritism, report suspicions, and never tip off a customer about a report.

scenes.heading: Confidentiality
scenes.narration: Customer information belongs to the institution and stays confidential during employment and after leaving.

cards.title: Gift or problem?
cards.prompt: Sort each case under the gifts and hospitality section of SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics.

items.text: A crystal trophy given at an official industry event
Cash from a customer whose loan you approved
Shares offered by a supplier bidding for a bank contract
A conference fee waiver that builds knowledge, with no conflict
A gift card from a customer who wants faster approval
A prize from a recognised, published award programme, with prior approval

cards.question: A branch employee receives a perishable gift hamper worth about SAR 1,500 from a corporate client at an official event. What do SAMA's principles require?
options: Nothing, because perishable gifts are always exempt
A written disclosure form to Compliance right after receiving it
Returning it within thirty days
Approval from the client's relationship manager
cards.explanation: The principles require a written disclosure to Compliance directly after receipt if the gift has a value and can be sold, or if it is perishable and worth more than SAR 1,000.

cards.title: SAMA's information classes
cards.caption: From Section III.G of the Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics. Requests from regulators go through Compliance.

items.label: Highly confidential
items.detail: Could significantly affect the institution, staff or stakeholders; authorised employees only.

items.label: Confidential
items.detail: All non-public information on the institution, staff or stakeholders; shared only as needed.

items.label: Insider
items.detail: Not disclosed to anyone outside the institution.

items.label: General
items.detail: Publicly available through authorised channels.

cards.title: Control and awareness measures for branch and customer service staff

items.label: Joining
items.detail: Declaration on secure-use, username and password policies.

items.label: Every three months
items.detail: Confidentiality campaign: customer account information and penalties.

items.label: Every three months
items.detail: Information security and fraud prevention campaign.

items.label: Every six months
items.detail: Test or survey to measure awareness.

items.label: Every year
items.detail: Renewed declaration; at most every two years, an audit or compliance review.

cards.title: The cousin and the balance
cards.situation: Review of the Jeddah case finds the clearing clerk could see full customer balances, the branch's last confidentiality campaign was seven months ago, and no staff test has been run this year. The customer has filed a complaint.

choices.text: Log and resolve the complaint, restrict the clerk's access to need-to-know, handle the breach under the disciplinary policy, restart three-monthly campaigns and run a staff test now.
choices.outcome: Best. It fixes the customer issue, the access control, the individual breach and the awareness gaps against SAMA's measures.

choices.text: Discipline the clerk and close the matter.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Accountability matters, but the access design and missed campaigns and tests would let it happen again.

choices.text: Send the branch an email reminding staff to be discreet.
choices.outcome: Poor. A one-off email does not meet the three-monthly campaigns, six-monthly tests or need-to-know access controls.

choices.text: Tell the customer family matters are outside the bank's control.
choices.outcome: Poor. The bank is responsible for protecting consumer information under Rule 11, and the complaint must be handled.

cards.back: Only the documents you are working on on the desk; others locked away; devices off and drawers locked when you leave.
Never discuss sensitive information in lifts, corridors or public transport.
Access customer data only within your powers and for work reasons.
The duty of confidentiality continues after employment ends.
Do not photograph or record confidential information with personal devices.
Answer supervisory requests only through Compliance or with authority.

cards.title: Real practice: publishing SAMA penalties
cards.body:
Since SAMA's 2017 **Instructions for Publishing Banking Penalties**, banks must show in their **annual reports** a section on SAMA punitive decisions: the subject of each violation, the number of decisions and the total fines in riyals, for the current and the previous financial year. SAMA said it will publish the reported violations on its own website.

One of the set subjects is **violation of SAMA's customer protection instructions**. Others cover supervisory instructions, due diligence, ATM and POS performance, and AML/CFT due diligence.

The lesson: consumer protection failures at the counter, in the call centre or in collection do not stay private. They can appear in the bank's published annual report, in front of shareholders, investors and customers.

cards.title: Evidence for a SAMA review
cards.prompt: Match each requirement to the evidence that proves it.

pairs.right: Training plans and attendance for front-line staff, including agency staff
Certificate register showing at least 90% coverage within a year of joining
Visit reports and semi-annual reports to senior management
Three-monthly campaign materials, six-monthly test results, signed declarations
Board-approved policy and proof that collectors and agencies know it
Signed principles in each employee's file

cards.question: How often must branch and customer service staff be tested or surveyed on the effectiveness of confidentiality and security awareness under SAMA's 2021 measures?
options: Every three months
At least every six months
Once a year
Every two years
cards.explanation: Campaigns run at least every three months; tests or surveys of employees take place at least every six months to assess how well the awareness works.

cards.title: Before the review team arrives
cards.body:
- Match every front-line name, including agency staff, to a certificate status and a joining date.
- Pull the last two semi-annual monitoring reports and the actions taken.
- Show campaign dates for each quarter and the latest six-monthly test results.
- Check that every employee file holds the signed conduct principles and current declarations.
- Bring the collection policy with its approval, review date and agency awareness proof.
- Pick three complaints and show the reference text, timeline and final answer.

cards.title: Vault of Trust take-aways
items: Conduct principles apply to everyone from board to third-party staff; managers ensure they are read, signed and filed.
Gifts: never cash, loans, shares or derivatives; disclose saleable gifts and perishable gifts above SAR 1,000 to Compliance.
Customer information is confidential during and after employment; access is need-to-know.
Branch and customer service staff: campaigns every three months, tests every six months, declarations on joining and every year.
SAMA penalties for customer protection violations appear in banks' annual reports, so evidence of training, monitoring and audit matters.

cards.prompt: If a SAMA reviewer asked you tomorrow to prove you understand the customer protection rules for your role, what evidence could you show, and what is missing?

quiz.question: Who do SAMA's Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics apply to?
options: Only employees in customer-facing roles
Only senior executives and board members
Only staff on permanent employment contracts, not contractors or consultants
All staff, from the board to consultants and third-party staff
quiz.explanation: The definition of staff covers board and committee members, executives, regular or contract employees, consultants and third-party employees.

quiz.question: What must managers do with the Principles of Conduct and Work Ethics for each employee?
options: Email them to the employee once a year
Post them on the branch notice board only
Make sure they are read, signed and kept in the employee's file
Keep them with the compliance team so they are ready for SAMA audits
quiz.explanation: Section I.B makes all managers responsible for ensuring the principles are read, signed and enclosed in the employee file, and the institution explains them on joining.

quiz.question: Which kind of gift may staff never accept, even at an official event?
options: A trophy given under event protocol
A fee waiver for a learning conference
A prize from a published award programme
Cash, a loan, shares or a financial derivative
quiz.explanation: Even where refusal would be offensive, an accepted gift must not be cash, a loan, shares or a financial derivative.

quiz.question: How often must banks run awareness campaigns on confidentiality of customer account information for branch and customer service staff?
options: At least every three months
At least every six months
At least once a year
When staff join the bank
quiz.explanation: The 2021 control and awareness measures require these campaigns, with continuing material, at least every three months.

quiz.question: When must branch and customer service staff sign a declaration on the secure-use, username and password policies?
options: When they start work and every year after that
Only when they are first hired
After every failed login attempt
Each time a campaign is completed
quiz.explanation: The measures require a paper or electronic declaration from employees both on starting work and annually.

quiz.question: How long must access logs for employees' use of bank account information be kept under SAMA's 2021 measures?
options: At least one year
At least ten years
At least five years
Until the employee leaves
quiz.explanation: Access information must be saved automatically for at least five years, including employee name and number, IP address, date and time, authority, authentication and action.

quiz.question: A clearing clerk can see full customer balances that his work does not need. Which control does SAMA's 2021 measures point to?
