options: Restrict access on a need-to-know basis, e.g. hide balances
Change his password every three months
Lock his account after three failed logins
Restrict his access to banking systems outside official working hours
quiz.explanation: The measures require restricting access to devices and systems on a need-to-know basis, with hiding customer balances from staff who don't need them as an example.

quiz.question: What does Rule 11 of the consumer protection rules require of temporary and third-party staff?
options: They are exempt if supervised by permanent staff
They sign the consumer information confidentiality form
They may work only with anonymised customer data, never with real records
They sign a form only when they leave the bank
quiz.explanation: Rule 11(b) requires all permanent and temporary employees and third-party employees, on the job or after leaving, to sign the confidentiality form.

quiz.question: Under SAMA's 2017 instructions, where must banks publish SAMA's punitive decisions?
options: Only in confidential reports to the board and to SAMA's supervision team
In their annual reports, by subject, number and total fines
In a notice displayed in every branch
On SAMA's website, uploaded by the bank
quiz.explanation: Banks must publish a 'SAMA Punitive Decisions' section in their annual reports with the subject, number of decisions and total fines; SAMA publishes the reported violations on its website.

quiz.question: A regulator's staff member phones a teller asking for a customer's account details. What do the conduct principles require?
options: Answer at once because regulators have authority
Refer the request to the Compliance Department
Ask the customer to call the regulator directly
Send the details by personal email for speed
quiz.explanation: Requests from supervisory authorities are referred to Compliance; no employee responds unless through Compliance or with authority to do so.

bank.question: Which law gives SAMA the duty to develop instructions and procedures that protect consumers of financial institutions, as cited in the 2022 principles?
options: The Personal Data Protection Law
The Credit Information Law
The Saudi Central Bank Law
The Law of Payments and Payment Services
bank.explanation: The principles cite Article 4 of the Saudi Central Bank Law, which lists developing consumer protection instructions among SAMA's powers. The other laws are cited for specific sectors.

bank.question: Sarawat Bank outsources its card call centre. A complaint shows an agent misled a customer. Which principle settles who is responsible?
options: Competition: customers could have chosen another bank
Outsourcing: the bank is not exempted from responsibility
Disclosure: the agent's firm must publish its own terms
Conflict of interest: the agent's firm must report it
bank.explanation: Principle 9 says the institution remains responsible when an outsourced provider deals with consumers, and is not exempted if the provider breaches the rules.

bank.question: A new joiner at the Riyadh call centre came through a staffing agency eight months ago and has not started the retail banking fundamentals certificate. What is the most accurate view?
options: She is exempt because agency staff are not employees of the bank itself
She needs the credit adviser certificate instead
She has until her third year of service to certify
She must be certified within four months to meet the one-year limit
bank.explanation: Call-centre staff, including those contracted through a third party, need the retail banking fundamentals certificate within one year of employment. Eight months have passed, so four remain.

bank.question: Rule 15 monitoring visits find that collection agency staff do not know SAMA's instructions. What does the rule expect next?
options: Wait for SAMA to inspect the collection agency directly before taking any action
Record the findings only in the agency's own files
Drop agency staff from the monitoring programme
Report them to senior management in the semi-annual report and act
bank.explanation: Rule 15 covers collection staff including third-party employees, and requires semi-annual reports to senior management to monitor performance; findings must lead to action.

bank.question: Which pairing of staff and certificate matches SAMA's October 2022 circular?
options: Call-centre agent: credit adviser only
Branch manager: both retail banking fundamentals and credit adviser
Customer care employee: no certificate needed
Retail credit officer: retail banking fundamentals only, not credit adviser
bank.explanation: Branch managers appear in both lists: front-line staff and their managers need retail banking fundamentals, and branch managers also need the credit adviser certificate.

bank.question: Which statement about the purpose of SAMA's 2022 principles is accurate?
options: They align with the international high-level consumer principles
They replace the Banking Control Law for all retail customers in the Kingdom
They apply only to banks and not to finance companies
They set maximum interest rates for consumer lending
bank.explanation: One stated purpose is to keep pace with the international High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection. They apply to all SAMA-supervised institutions and do not replace the Banking Control Law.

bank.question: Which principle requires a written policy and procedures to identify transactions likely to create a conflict of interest?
options: Principle 4
Principle 6
Principle 10
Principle 2
bank.explanation: Principle 10 on conflict of interest requires a written policy and procedures for identifying transactions that may cause a conflict.

bank.question: A front-line employee holds the retail banking certificate but has had no training since joining four years ago. The bank argues the certificate is enough under Rule 14. Which reply is strongest?
options: Rule 14 asks only for a certificate, so the bank is already fully compliant
Rule 14 applies only to staff in their first year
Rule 14 is met if a mystery shopper visit was passed
Rule 14 requires both certificates and training on a regular basis
bank.explanation: Rule 14 combines two duties: regular training for front-line staff and the necessary professional certificates. Holding one does not replace the other.

bank.question: Under SAMA's 2020 announcement, what should a customer do before complaining to SAMA's Consumer Protection Department?
options: Wait sixty days after the incident
Obtain a lawyer's opinion on the case
File a police report on the matter
Contact the bank or company first
bank.explanation: SAMA's announcement asked customers to contact their bank or company first, and to complain to SAMA if it did not cooperate.

bank.question: A borrower asks for a detailed amortisation schedule showing all fees and costs. What do the specific conduct rules require of a bank?
options: Provide it free within one business day, once, on request
Provide it within five working days for a set fee
Provide it only when the loan is fully repaid
Provide it only if the customer is in default
bank.explanation: Specific Rule 5 requires a detailed schedule free of charge within one business day on request, once, in case of default or early payment.

bank.question: A customer finishes paying off her personal loan. What must the bank do about a clearance letter?
options: Issue it within thirty days, once she submits a written request for it
Issue it only if she pays an administration fee
Issue it immediately through a documented channel, unasked
Issue it only after a credit bureau update
bank.explanation: Specific Rule 3 requires banks to issue a clearance letter immediately after payment through a documented channel without a request, except where judicial decisions apply.

bank.question: A text message with a one-time password says only 'Your OTP is 4821'. Which rule does it fall short of?
options: Rule 12, which requires the OTP's purpose to be stated
Rule 6, which sets a minimum font size for contracts
Rule 9, which requires a published fee list
Rule 26, which covers branch working hours
bank.explanation: Rule 12(b) requires OTP messages to state their purpose, such as adding a beneficiary, resetting a password or transferring money.

bank.question: When a customer applies for a product, which items must the immediate text message contain at a minimum?
options: Subject, reference number, expected date and toll-free number
Product price, credit score and branch address
The approval decision, the interest rate and the full schedule of fees
Manager's name, SAMA's number and a survey link
bank.explanation: Rule 10(a) lists the application subject, reference number, expected implementation date and the toll-free number for inquiries.

bank.question: A debit card expires on 30 June. Under the specific conduct rules, by when should the bank reissue it unless the customer asks otherwise?
options: At least 30 days before expiry, by 31 May
On the expiry date itself
Within 30 days after expiry
At least 90 days before expiry
bank.explanation: Specific Rule 11 requires debit cards to be reissued at least 30 days before the expiry date unless the consumer requests otherwise.

bank.question: An applicant brings incomplete documents to open an account. What does the account opening timeline rule require?
options: Reject the application with no reason given
Open the account and request documents later
Inform the applicant in writing of the missing items
Ask the applicant to apply at another branch
bank.explanation: The rule on timelines says the applicant must be informed in writing of any missing or additional requirements upon application.

bank.question: A customer wants a new account but cannot visit the branch because of an illness beyond her control. What may the bank do?
options: Send two or more staff with different powers to meet her
Open the account by phone with no ID check
Ask a relative to sign the account opening forms on her behalf at the branch
Refuse until she can attend the branch
bank.explanation: The Account Opening Rules allow, in exceptional cases, two or more staff with different powers to meet the customer on site and collect the required information and documents.

bank.question: Sarawat Bank's credit card team issues cards on the basis of pre-approved offers that customers never request. Which combination of rules does this most clearly breach?
options: Cards only on a documented request, and no annual fee before activation
Cards only after a branch visit, and annual fees fixed for the first five years
Cards only for salaried staff, and fees approved by SAMA
Cards only with a guarantor, and statements sent by post
bank.explanation: Specific Rule 14 requires cards to be issued on a request through documented channels and bars annual fees before activation; the issuer may cancel cards not activated within 90 days.

bank.question: Where must a bank display its list of fees and commissions, including third-party fees?
options: Only in the contract annexes
Only on request at the counter
In the head office and branches, and on its websites
Only in the annual report
bank.explanation: Rule 9 requires the list to be displayed visibly in the head office and branches and published on the websites.

bank.question: How often must a bank's complaint-handling performance indicators for directly filed complaints be reported to the highest executive under Rule 20?
options: Monthly
Quarterly
Semi-annually
Annually
bank.explanation: Rule 20 requires indicators such as customer satisfaction and complaint handling quality, with results reported quarterly to the highest executive position.

bank.question: A complaint involves a SAR 15,000 refund. Under SAMA's 2023 regulations, who can decide it without escalating further?
options: Only the chief executive officer
Only the board's audit committee
The Customer Care Department manager or delegate
Only SAMA's consumer protection department
bank.explanation: The department manager or delegate has full authority to resolve complaints of amounts not exceeding SAR 20,000, under policies the bank sets.

bank.question: Which three units must a bank's Customer Care Department contain at a minimum?
options: Complaints Handling; Collections and Recoveries; Marketing, Sales and Cross-selling Support
Complaints Handling; Quality and Performance Analysis; Awareness and Education
Compliance, Internal Audit and Legal Affairs
Call Centre, Branch Network and Digital Channels
bank.explanation: The 2023 regulations require at least these three units, sized to the bank's business volume and customer numbers.

bank.question: What qualification must Customer Care Department staff hold at a minimum under SAMA's 2023 regulations?
options: A law degree and a compliance diploma
An internal audit certification
Retail banking and credit advisory certificates
A cyber security awareness badge
bank.explanation: Department managers and staff must hold at least the basic retail banking and credit advisory certificates, and receive relevant training at least once a year.

bank.question: A wheelchair user reaches the branch and finds the self-service kiosk mounted too high. Which SAMA instruction applies most directly?
options: The account opening rule on customer presence
The built-environment duty for persons with disabilities
The rule on displaying branch working hours
The rule on ATM maintenance and monitoring
bank.explanation: SAMA's instructions for persons with disabilities require suitable premises, including kiosks equipped and placed at a height that eases their use.

bank.question: A finance officer turns down a loan applicant 'because, with her disability, she might stop working'. She meets all credit criteria. Which assessment is best?
options: Exclusion on disability grounds without a legal basis is forbidden
It is lawful because credit risk is the bank's own decision
It is lawful as long as the reason is stated clearly in the rejection text message
It is lawful if a medical report confirms the disability
bank.explanation: The instructions forbid excluding or restricting access to a service because of disability without a legal basis, and Rule 24 forbids discrimination on disability.

bank.question: Which body must review and audit a bank's Customer Care Department every year?
options: SAMA's on-site inspection team
The Internal Audit and Compliance Departments
An external ISO auditor only
The retail banking business head
bank.explanation: The final provisions require an annual review and audit by Internal Audit and Compliance; separately, the department holds ISO 10002 certification renewed annually.

bank.question: Under Principle 3, what must the institution develop for consumers?
options: Loyalty schemes that reward long-standing customers
Marketing campaigns for new financial products
Discounts for customers who never complain
Programmes that build knowledge and help informed decisions
bank.explanation: Principle 3 on education and awareness requires programmes and mechanisms that raise consumers' knowledge and skills, explain major risks and support informed decisions.

bank.question: An older customer with limited reading skills is offered a credit card at the counter. Which approach best fits SAMA's principles and rules?
options: Give the form and ask him to read it at home
Sign him up quickly to save him a second visit
Ask his son, who came with him, to read and sign the form on his father's behalf today
Explain terms and risks, check he understands, record his acknowledgement
bank.explanation: Principle 1 calls for special attention to older and less educated customers, and Rules 1 and 5 require encouraging reading, checking understanding and obtaining acknowledgement of the disclosure form.

bank.question: A borrower with a monthly-instalment loan has paid nothing for three consecutive months. How do the 2025 regulations classify this?
options: As a potential default only, until six months pass
As a complaint case requiring SAMA's review
As default under Article 9's definition
As a total disability case under Article 11
bank.explanation: For monthly instalments, default includes failing to pay fully or partly for three consecutive months; other tests cover repeated late payments.

bank.question: A salaried borrower's salary is deposited on the 27th. On the 24th the bank deducts his instalment, which is due on the 27th. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, if the account balance was sufficient
Deducting before the agreed due date is prohibited
Nothing, if he was notified by text message
Only that it was not done at a branch
bank.explanation: Article 8 forbids deducting the instalment before the agreed due date or withholding it before then; deduction dates follow the salary deposit date.

bank.question: A borrower's salary arrives late because of a public holiday, and the bank deducts two instalments in the next salary cycle without his consent. Which rule is breached?
options: The ban on deducting end-of-service gratuities of Saudi nationals without consent
The ban on taking more than one instalment per salary cycle per contract
The ban on calling relatives of the borrower
The cap of one instalment on total delay fees
bank.explanation: Article 8 prohibits deducting more than one instalment per finance contract in a single salary deposit cycle without a court order or the consumer's consent; Article 7 also asks creditors to allow for holiday shifts.

bank.question: A Saudi borrower retires and his end-of-service gratuity reaches his account. May the bank withhold it to clear his loan?
options: Yes, because the gratuity is a deposit like any other
Yes, if the loan is more than ninety days overdue
No, gratuities may never be used for any debt
No, unless there is a court order or his consent
bank.explanation: Article 8 forbids withholding or deducting a national consumer's end-of-service gratuity unless there is a judicial order or ruling, or the consumer consents.

bank.question: The bank learns that a borrower died. When must it complete the exemption procedures under Article 11?
options: Within 30 days after the insurer pays out
Within 90 days of the date of death
Within 30 days of receiving the death certificate
After the heirs file a written complaint
bank.explanation: Creditors must complete exemption within thirty days of receiving the death certificate or disability report, without making it depend on the insurer's approval.

bank.question: Which language is the primary language for collection communications under Article 5?
options: English for all written messages
Arabic, except with non-Arabic speakers
The language of the finance contract
Any language the agency chooses
bank.explanation: Article 5 sets Arabic as the primary language, except when communicating with non-Arabic speakers.

bank.question: A borrower defaulted because the bank lent him beyond the statutory deduction ratio. He asks for help. What do the 2025 regulations require?
options: Reschedule without new finance, extra fees or a change in the term cost
Offer a top-up loan at a lower interest rate to clear the arrears in one step
Reschedule but allow a higher term cost
Refer him to the courts before any rescheduling
bank.explanation: Article 9(2-2) requires rescheduling where the cause is the creditor's failure to assess creditworthiness, such as exceeding statutory deduction ratios, without new finance, fees or a term-cost change.

bank.question: What must a collection phone call allow the consumer to do at the end of the call?
options: Make a payment by card on the spot
Speak to a manager about the bank's products
Choose a new repayment date by keypad
Rate their satisfaction, recorded electronically
bank.explanation: Article 4 requires creditors to let consumers or guarantors evaluate their satisfaction at the end of the call, whether for collection or complaints, and to document it electronically.

bank.question: An employee overhears that a listed company client will announce a merger and tells a friend to buy its shares. Which section of SAMA's conduct principles is breached?
options: Gifts and hospitality
Remuneration and compensation
Interaction with stakeholders
Use and leakage of insider information
bank.explanation: Section III.H forbids using or leaking insider information to obtain benefits for oneself or others, and Section III.G treats such information as confidential.

bank.question: Under SAMA's conduct principles, when may AML/CFT tasks be assigned to an employee?
options: After six months in a customer-facing role
After reading the AML policy and signing it
Only after specialised, accredited AML/CFT courses
Only after a SAMA examination is passed
bank.explanation: Section III.C.1 says AML/CFT tasks are assigned only after the employee joins specialised and accredited AML/CFT courses.

bank.question: An employee reports suspected fraud by a colleague in good faith. Under Section III.I, what must the institution do?
options: Reveal the reporter's name to the colleague so the investigation is fair to both
Ask the reporter to prove the fraud before acting
Protect the reporter's confidentiality and tolerate no retaliation
Move the reporter to another branch for safety
bank.explanation: The whistleblowing section requires protecting whistleblowers' confidentiality and good-faith reporters, and not tolerating retaliation; staff who deliberately ignore wrongdoing are held accountable.

bank.question: A branch employee enters the wrong banking system password three times in a row. What happens under SAMA's 2021 measures?
options: The username is suspended until restored under bank procedures
The password is reset automatically by text
The branch manager must log in and re-enter the password on the employee's behalf
Nothing until the fifth failed attempt
bank.explanation: The measures require suspension after three consecutive wrong entries, restored only under the bank's internal procedures.

bank.question: How often must a bank have Internal Audit or Compliance review its compliance with the branch and customer service control and awareness measures?
options: Every three months
Every six months
Only after a data breach
Periodically, within a maximum of two years
bank.explanation: The general provisions assign Internal Audit or Compliance to examine compliance periodically, within a maximum of two years.

bank.question: Sarawat Bank runs confidentiality campaigns twice a year and tests staff once a year. A reviewer asks if this meets SAMA's measures. Which answer is right?
options: Yes: two campaigns and one staff test each year meet SAMA's stated minimum frequency
No: campaigns every three months and tests every six months, at least
No: campaigns are monthly and tests quarterly
Yes: frequency is left entirely to the bank's policy
bank.explanation: The 2021 measures require campaigns at least every three months and tests or surveys at least every six months, so the bank is short on both.

bank.question: What should an employee do with confidential documents they are not using at the moment, under the conduct principles?
options: Leave them stacked on the desk for quick access
Keep them in drawers, preferably locked
Take them home to finish work in the evening
Photograph them on a phone for easier reference
bank.explanation: Staff should keep only current documents on the desk and others in drawers, preferably locked; copying outside the building needs approval and personal recording is banned.

bank.question: Which subject category in SAMA's instructions for publishing banking penalties would capture fines for breaching the consumer protection rules?
options: Violation of SAMA's customer protection instructions
Violation of SAMA's supervisory instructions
Violation of SAMA's ATM and POS performance instructions
Violation of SAMA's AML/CTF due diligence instructions
bank.explanation: The instructions list several subjects; customer protection violations have their own category, separate from supervisory, ATM/POS and AML/CTF categories.
